newsitem.title: USA: Big week expected for new U.S. junk bond issuance.
newsitem.headline: Big week expected for new U.S. junk bond issuance.

text.p: The primary market for U.S. high-yield bonds may experience one of its busiest periods in recent memory, with $1.9 billion in new issues expected to price this week, dealers say.
By comparison, new supply in the investment-grade new-issue volume is expected to taper off from last week's heavy levels, according to sydnicate officials
Market players were expecting issuers to bring $1.9 billion in new high-yield paper this week, most coming in the form of 144a private placement deals.
"Any time we have an election, issuers try to tap the market beforehand, becuase they don't know what the market will look like afterwards," a syndicate official said.

In what may be the largest deal to hit the market this week, International Home Foods plans to sell $400 million in high-yield paper in a 144a deal during the middle of the week through Chase Securities Inc, market players say.

Unison Healthcare is also expected to debut in the high-yield market today with a $100 million 144a deal through CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc. Price talk on the deal is 10 1/2 percent to 10 3/4 percent, sources say.

Other expected issuers this week include Blue Chip Casinos Inc, which plans to sell $95 million in senior secured debt due 2003 through Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp; Coca-Cola FEMSA SA, a Mexican bottler, with a $175 million deal through J.P. Morgan and Co Inc; and National Energy Group with a $100 million deal through Bear Stearns.
Turning to the U.S. high-grade primary market, the bulk of activity is expected to come from foreign issuers.
Pohang Iron & Steel is likely to issue $300 million in 10-year debt securities via Salomon Brothers Inc.
Syndicate officials say GTE North, a unit of GTE Corp, also plans to sell $250 million in 12-year maturity debt in a competitive bid offering later in the week.
Among domestic issuers, Levi Strauss & Co is also scheduled to hit the market mid-week with a 144a offering through Goldman Sachs & Co, sources say.
